data.why: The repo ships no example .xvg data (only inline byte-string fixtures in tests/), so synthetic GROMACS-style RMSD/Rg/RMSF files were written matching the app's filename-based auto-detection and column expectations, including an equilibration curve, a transient outlier spike, a corrupted data row, a second run for Welch t-test comparison, and an empty/failed file.

goals: Upload RMSD and Rg traces from a simulation and judge whether the system has equilibrated before trusting later statistics
Spot per-residue flexibility hotspots (e.g. a flexible loop or disordered tail) in an RMSF profile
Check whether a designed structural feature (e.g. a rigid linker) shows the expected low fluctuation relative to the rest of the protein
Get a heuristic quality/stability score to triage a run quickly before deeper, publication-grade analysis
Statistically compare two runs (e.g. wild-type vs. a mutant/redesign) on the same metric with a Welch t-test
Export the parsed data, chart images, and a Markdown/PDF report to share or archive the triage results

review.summary: The tree matches the README's stated purpose closely: triage RMSD/Rg for equilibration, check that the designed linker is rigid in RMSF, compare wild-type and mutant with a caveated Welch test, and export. Its labels are clean and every cited screen I opened supports its node. It needs light fixes before filing: split the Q&A explainer out of the analysis-card feature, demote two UI-mechanic tasks, promote the visual run overlay to its own task, and caveat the spike-driven 14/100 score and the ps-only equilibration units.
